messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 57 omitted, sha256 2093762f9e6cde05>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Entailment
confidence: 72
reason: Clause 3.2 requires return or destruction of confidential information on request but expressly lets PwC, as a receiving party, keep a copy for its internal purposes, which supports the hypothesis for that party.
<quote check="exact">PwC may retain a copy of the confidential information for our internal purposes.</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Entailment
confidence: 90
reason: Clause 3.2 requires return or destruction of confidential information but expressly lets PwC, as a receiving party, keep a copy for internal purposes.
<quote check="exact">However, PwC may retain a copy of the confidential information for our internal purposes.</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Entailment
confidence: 80
reason: Although the receiving party must return or destroy confidential information on request, PwC as receiving party may keep a copy for internal purposes, and electronic copies need only be made reasonably inaccessible.
<quote check="exact">However, PwC may retain a copy of the confidential information for our internal purposes.</quote>
<quote check="exact">delete them or make them reasonably inaccessible</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Entailment", "confidence": 85, "quotes": ["However, PwC may retain a copy of the confidential information for our internal purposes."], "reason": "Clause 3.2 lets PwC, when it is the receiving party, keep a copy of confidential information for internal purposes even after return or destruction is requested."}
